versions.changelog: Fix runtime namespace resolution so alternate published slugs load the correct project .image-skills config.
Stabilize project-scoped env loading and improve the article illustration workflow.
Align runtime config loading and safer image batch defaults.
Fix setup namespace defaults after install.

- Internal setup script updated in scripts/setup.mjs.
- No user-facing workflow or interface changes.
- All usage, features, and documentation remain unchanged.

- Added shared image generation vendor scripts and reference config files under scripts/vendor/shared-image-generation/.
- Introduced setup, configuration, and model registry schema documentation for first-time skill usage.
- Added workflow tools including bootstrap, doctor, ensure-ready, smoke-check, and model discovery scripts to streamline environment readiness and model recommendations.
- No breaking changes to core illustration workflow; main update is improved tooling and configuration support.

Version 9.0.0 — Major workflow and documentation update for illustration generation.

- Rewritten and expanded documentation for end-to-end illustration pipelines, including use cases, example commands, and workflow steps.
- Clarifies requirements for reference images (must be public URLs; no local paths/data URLs).
- Details structured approach to illustration type, style, and density decisions.
- Documents bundled scripts for scaffolding, prompt-building, batch generation, and Markdown insertion.
- Emphasizes best practices for article analysis, prompt consistency, and visually coherent multi-image outputs.
- Improved safety, security, and environment variable handling guidance.

**Major internal restructuring and simplification of the runtime vendor dependencies.**

- Replaced previous `vendor/generation-runtime` system with a slimmed-down, direct vendor of only essential `weryai-image`, `weryai-core`, and `compression-runtime` scripts under `scripts/vendor/`.
- Removed legacy, unused, or documentation-heavy files from vendor directories, reducing clutter and maintenance overhead.
- Updated CLI interface and documentation: image generation is now directly accessible via `npm run generate`, replacing previous indirection and making the workflow simpler.
- Improved skill manifest: environment and binary requirements are now more clearly defined.
- Internal scripts have been reorganized for easier maintenance; overhead from extraneous bootstrap logic is eliminated.
- No functional changes to illustration workflow or features—usage and capabilities unchanged for end-users.

**Added support for env var checks and improved setup/quickstart workflow.**

- The skill now declares required environment variables (`IMAGE_GEN_API_KEY`) for better setup guidance.
- Updated `SKILL.md` with a Quickstart section and environment variable documentation.
- Safety section now clarifies environment variable storage and process execution policies.
- Scripts and health checks improved under the hood for environment and dependency readiness.
- No breaking changes to generation logic.

- Adds clear requirements and guidance for reference images: only public URLs (HTTPS strongly recommended), local and data URLs not supported.
- Expands the "Safety & Scope" section explaining network usage, authentication, file outputs, and security boundaries.
- Documents new restrictions on reference image formats and accessibility for generation tasks.
- Ensures users are aware of best practices for successful multi-illustration, consistent article workflows.

Initial release of article-illustrator.

- Generate multiple, coordinated illustrations for articles with structured type and style selection.
- Automatically analyzes article structure to identify optimal illustration positions.
- Supports initializing outlines, building prompts, generating images in batch, and inserting image references in Markdown.
- Ensures consistent look and feel across multiple illustrations with a shared series reference.
- Bundles scripts for the entire workflow, including prompt creation, batch file generation, and output compression.
- Optimized for tutorials, reviews, and multi-section articles—not for single cover images or infographics.
